prompt: During our cooking class, the chef told me I (can) taste the soup.
explanation_ru: После глагола в прошедшем времени (told) модальный глагол can в косвенной речи меняется на could.

prompt: The taxi driver told us we (must) pay cash for that short ride.
explanation_ru: Для передачи долженствования в прошедшей ситуации модальный глагол must в косвенной речи переходит в had to.

prompt: In her email, the school secretary wrote that the dentist (may) visit soon.
explanation_ru: После вводящего глагола в прошедшем времени (wrote) модальный глагол may меняется на might.

prompt: Before dinner, Rafael's father told him he (should) invite his sister too.
explanation_ru: Модальный глагол should в косвенной речи не изменяется, даже если вводящий глагол стоит в прошедшем времени.

prompt: At the station office, the clerk mentioned I (might) find my red scarf.
explanation_ru: Модальный глагол might при переводе в косвенную речь остаётся без изменений.

prompt: Laughing, the dog walker told Mateo his dog (could) chase that ball forever.
explanation_ru: Модальный глагол could в косвенной речи не меняется после глагола в прошедшем времени.

prompt: Leaving the Glasgow job centre, Ciara asked the adviser when she (will) hear back from the company.
explanation_ru: В косвенном вопросе после глагола в прошедшем времени (asked) глагол will сдвигается в would.

prompt: My dental appointment in Athens was at nine. The receptionist told me I (have to) arrive fifteen minutes early.
explanation_ru: Конструкция have to в косвенной речи после told переходит в прошедшую форму had to.

prompt: The old clock looked overpriced. At the Berlin market, the seller still insisted I (ought to) buy it right away.
explanation_ru: Модальный глагол ought to, как и should, не изменяется при переводе в косвенную речь.

prompt: Freja wasn't sure about the second-hand lamp. The Copenhagen shop owner promised she could return it if she (to keep) the receipt.
explanation_ru: В условном предложении первого типа при передаче в косвенной речи глагол в части с if сдвигается из Present Simple в Past Simple (kept).

prompt: Traffic was building up along the coast in Cape Town. Our driver warned us that we would miss our train if we (to take) the longer road through the centre.
explanation_ru: В косвенной речи после warned условное предложение первого типа сдвигается на шаг назад, поэтому в части с if нужен Past Simple (took).

prompt: Amara felt nervous backstage before the audition. The drama coach reassured her that she (would) win the main part if she (to speak) louder and more slowly.
explanation_ru: В условном предложении второго типа при переводе в косвенную речь модальный глагол would и форма Past Simple (spoke) остаются без изменений.

prompt: Prices in the Milan museum shop were quite high. The assistant explained that visitors could not get a discount unless they (to show) a valid student card.
explanation_ru: В условном предложении первого типа после глагола в прошедшем времени (explained) глагол после unless переходит в Past Simple (showed).

prompt: I reached my small hotel in Kyoto too early for my room. The friendly desk clerk said I (can) leave my heavy bag at the front desk. He also promised it (will) stay safe there until evening.
explanation_ru: После вводящих глаголов в прошедшем времени (said, promised) модальные глаголы can и will в косвенной речи меняются на could и would.

prompt: Music filled the whole square during the street parade in Salvador. A helpful volunteer explained that we (could) walk beside the loud trucks along the main street. However, she warned that everyone (should / not) cross the yellow safety rope.
explanation_ru: Модальные глаголы could и should (в том числе в отрицании shouldn't) при согласовании времён в косвенной речи не изменяются.

prompt: Before lunch ended at the Shenzhen canteen, the head cook spoke to Wei in the kitchen. He worried that the rice (may) run out before the evening shift. He asked what they (shall) do if another big group arrived. Wei quickly replied that they (have to) order extra bags right away.
explanation_ru: После глаголов в прошедшем времени may переходит в might, shall в вопросе о действиях — в should, а have to — в had to.

prompt: Sofia stepped onto the crowded tram in Lisbon and tapped her travel card. The ticket inspector checked the screen and told her she (must) buy a full paper ticket because her pass had run out. She wondered if the machine would take coins if she (to find) enough change in her bag. Luckily, a kind passenger lent her two euros.
explanation_ru: Обязательство в прошедшей ситуации передаётся через had to вместо must, а в условной части с if глагол сдвигается в Past Simple (found).

prompt: Strong winds were forecast for Auckland harbour over the weekend. The port officer emailed Lachlan to say he (might) need to move his small boat to a safer corner. He added that the old ropes (would / not) hold if the wind (to come) directly from the south. Lachlan drove down to the water before sunset to check each knot.
explanation_ru: Модальные глаголы might и would (в отрицании wouldn't) в косвенной речи не меняются, а в условной части с if требуется Past Simple (came).

prompt: Heavy rain had turned the garden lawn into soft mud overnight. Thabo's mother reminded the children that they (need) to stay off the wet grass until it (to dry) completely in the sun. She warned them they would ruin their clean trainers if they (to run) across the yard before noon. They grumbled, then decided to play board games inside instead.
explanation_ru: После глаголов в прошедшем времени (reminded, warned) need to переходит в needed to, глагол в придаточном времени — в dried, а в условной части с if нужен Past Simple (ran).

prompt: We lost our first doubles match in Buenos Aires by only two points. Walking off the court, my partner Camila admitted that we would have won the final set if we (to make) fewer mistakes. She added that we really (ought to) practise our serves before the weekend matches. I agreed and booked an empty court straight away.
explanation_ru: Условное предложение третьего типа (would have won + if ... had made) и модальный глагол ought to в косвенной речи сохраняют свои формы без изменений.

prompt: The chef in Vancouver told Tariq he ___ him prepare the fish.
explanation_ru: После глагола в прошедшем времени (told) can меняется на could, а частица to после модального глагола не ставится. Частая ошибка — оставить can без сдвига.

prompt: Before Monday's test, our lecturer said we ___ the new textbook.
explanation_ru: Для передачи обязательства в прошедшей ситуации must и have to в косвенной речи меняются на had to. Оставлять must или have to без сдвига ошибочно.

prompt: During the safety briefing in Antarctica, the scientist warned the new worker that she ___ outside alone, even in clear weather.
explanation_ru: Запрет mustn't в косвенной речи сохраняется. Частая ошибка — заменить его на didn't have to, но didn't have to означает отсутствие необходимости, а не запрет.

prompt: Everyone in the comments agreed with the TV review. It mentioned that new viewers ___ the first episode twice to follow the story.
explanation_ru: После глагола в прошедшем времени (mentioned) используется might + начальная форма глагола (might need). Ошибочно оставлять may или ставить после модального глагола форму needed.

prompt: Nadia was nervous before her piano exam in Vienna, so her teacher gently told her that she would feel calmer if she ___ the opening slowly.
explanation_ru: В условной части с if в косвенной речи нужен Past Simple (played). Частая ошибка — добавлять would внутрь придаточного с if или оставлять Present Simple (plays).

prompt: Last summer in Accra, my aunt told me I must call my parents.
answer: Last summer in Accra, my aunt told me I had to call my parents.
accepted_answers: Last summer in Accra, my aunt told me I had to call my parents.
Last summer in Accra, my aunt told me that I had to call my parents.
explanation_ru: Типичная ошибка — оставить must для обязательства в прошлом. После told в таком контексте нужно заменить must на had to.

prompt: A red error flashed on his screen. Still, the Tallinn developer promised he can finish the task.
answer: A red error flashed on his screen. Still, the Tallinn developer promised he could finish the task.
accepted_answers: A red error flashed on his screen. Still, the Tallinn developer promised he could finish the task.
A red error flashed on his screen. Still, the Tallinn developer promised that he could finish the task.
explanation_ru: Частая ошибка — забыть сдвинуть can после вводящего глагола в прошедшем времени (promised). Здесь требуется форма could.

prompt: Over morning coffee in the staffroom, our maths teacher complained that the new timetable might change again.
answer: Over morning coffee in the staffroom, our maths teacher complained that the new timetable might change again.
accepted_answers: Over morning coffee in the staffroom, our maths teacher complained that the new timetable might change again.
explanation_ru: Ошибки в предложении нет: модальный глагол might в косвенной речи не изменяется даже после глагола в прошедшем времени (complained).

prompt: Standing beside the ancient temple steps in Kyoto, the caretaker warned the tourists that they would slip easily if they would walk on the smooth wet stones.
answer: Standing beside the ancient temple steps in Kyoto, the caretaker warned the tourists that they would slip easily if they walked on the smooth wet stones.
accepted_answers: Standing beside the ancient temple steps in Kyoto, the caretaker warned the tourists that they would slip easily if they walked on the smooth wet stones.
Standing beside the ancient temple steps in Kyoto, the caretaker warned the tourists they would slip easily if they walked on the smooth wet stones.
explanation_ru: Частая ошибка — использовать would в условной части с if. После warned в косвенной речи здесь нужен Past Simple: if they walked.

prompt: Beside a hotel pool in Turkey, a lifeguard told a father, "Small children mustn't enter the deep end alone."
options: The lifeguard warned the father that small children didn't have to enter the deep end alone.
The lifeguard warned the father that small children mustn't enter the deep end alone.
The lifeguard warned the father that small children wouldn't enter the deep end alone.
The lifeguard warned the father that small children might not enter the deep end alone.
explanation_ru: Запрет mustn't в косвенной речи сохраняется. Вариант didn't have to меняет смысл на отсутствие необходимости, а wouldn't и might not передают прогноз или вероятность.

prompt: At an eye clinic in Cairo, the doctor told Karim, "You shouldn't wear these glasses while swimming, or you might lose them in the pool."
options: The doctor advised Karim that he didn't have to wear those glasses while swimming, or he could lose them.
The doctor advised Karim that he had to wear those glasses while swimming, or he might lose them.
The doctor advised Karim that he shouldn't wear those glasses while swimming, or he might lose them.
The doctor advised Karim that he shouldn't to wear those glasses while swimming, or he may lose them.
explanation_ru: В косвенной речи shouldn't и might не меняются, а these переходит в those. Замена shouldn't на didn't have to или had to искажает совет врача, а вариант с shouldn't to и may грамматически неверен.

prompt: On our video call, Mr Novak told me, "You must turn your camera on, or I can't mark you present." → On our video call, Mr Novak told me …
answer: On our video call, Mr Novak told me that I had to turn my camera on, or he couldn't mark me present.
accepted_answers: On our video call, Mr Novak told me that I had to turn my camera on, or he couldn't mark me present.
On our video call, Mr Novak told me I had to turn my camera on, or he couldn't mark me present.
On our video call, Mr Novak told me that I had to turn my camera on, or he could not mark me present.
On our video call, Mr Novak told me I had to turn my camera on, or he could not mark me present.
explanation_ru: После told глагол must переходит в had to, can't — в couldn't, а местоимения меняются по смыслу (you → I, your → my, I → he, you → me).
